instructions: Read one project-wide rule and the full text of one product spec. Does the spec trigger the rule? Answer yes when the spec makes a change the rule applies to, whether or not it meets the rule. Answer no when nothing the spec changes falls under the rule.

labels.name: yes
labels.description: The spec makes a change the rule applies to.

input.rule: When any change adds a screen or alters what a user can do, the change ships with its help center article.
input.spec: Saved filters. Users can save the current filter set under a name from the toolbar. Acceptance: when a user saves a filter, it appears in the saved list.

input.rule: Every new API endpoint is listed in the public changelog before release.
input.spec: Bulk tags. A new internal endpoint applies one tag to many items. Changelog: not needed, the endpoint is internal and never public.

input.rule: When a change alters what a human sees or does, its PR carries a QA evidence bundle before the merge ask.
input.spec: Rule notes. The review page shows a missed note when a spec skips a project rule. Acceptance: a spec that skips a rule shows one missed note. Evidence: seam tests behind fakes and a QA bundle on a real spec.

labels.name: no
labels.description: Nothing the spec changes falls under the rule.

input.rule: When any change adds a screen or alters what a user can do, the change ships with its help center article.
input.spec: Faster cache. The server keeps parsed templates in memory. Acceptance: a second render of one template does not read the disk.

input.rule: Every new API endpoint is listed in the public changelog before release.
input.spec: Dark theme. The settings page offers a dark theme toggle. Acceptance: toggling it switches every page to dark colors.
